target.title: fix(infra): use Buffer.byteLength for JSON string byte-limit fast-path guard
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`jsonStringByteLengthUpToLimit` in `src/infra/json-utf8-bytes.ts` uses `value.length` (UTF-16 code unit count) as a fast-path estimate of JSON-encoded byte size. For CJK text this underestimates the actual UTF-8 byte count by up to **3×** — `"中".repeat(100)` has `.length = 100` but `Buffer.byteLength = 300`.

The guard `value.length + 2 > remainingBytes` is meant to bail early when a string definitely won't fit in the remaining budget, avoiding the expensive `JSON.stringify` + `Buffer.byteLength` fallback. With CJK content, this guard incorrectly passes strings that should bail, wasting an allocation on every miss.

The accurate fallback (`jsonUtf8BytesOrInfinity`) still catches the overflow, so **no data corruption occurs**. But each miss triggers an unnecessary `JSON.stringify` allocation that the fast path was designed to prevent.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace `value.length` with `Buffer.byteLength(value, "utf8")`. `Buffer.byteLength` on a string is O(n) without allocating a buffer — still much cheaper than the `JSON.stringify` fallback it guards against.

`Buffer.byteLength` is already used elsewhere in the same file (lines 4, 6, 23), and the `+ 2` JSON-quote constant is preserved.

## User Impact

- `boundedJsonUtf8Bytes` fast-path bailout now works correctly for CJK and emoji content
- No behaviour change for ASCII text (`byteLength == length`)
- Callers unaffected: `session-tool-result-guard`, `worker-environments/inference`, `tool-result-middleware` — all 105 caller tests pass

## Evidence

**Environment**: Node.js v24.13.1, Linux x86_64, upstream/main at e9e62b563.

**Scenario**: `boundedJsonUtf8Bytes({value: "中".repeat(100)}, 200)` — the object is 302 JSON bytes, but the budget is only 200. The fast path should bail early:

```bash
node --import tsx -e '
import { Buffer } from "node:buffer";
const value = "中".repeat(100);
const remainingBytes = 190;  // after object framing overhead
// old guard
const oldBail = value.length + 2 > remainingBytes;
// new guard
const newBail = Buffer.byteLength(value, "utf8") + 2 > remainingBytes;
console.log("value:", value.length, "code units,", Buffer.byteLength(value, "utf8"), "UTF-8 bytes");
console.log("JSON actual:", Buffer.byteLength(JSON.stringify(value), "utf8"), "bytes");
console.log("budget:", remainingBytes, "bytes remaining");
console.log("old guard (length + 2):", value.length + 2, ">", remainingBytes, "=", oldBail);
console.log("new guard (byteLength + 2):", Buffer.byteLength(value, "utf8") + 2, ">", remainingBytes, "=", newBail);
'
```

```
value: 100 code units, 300 UTF-8 bytes
JSON actual: 302 bytes
budget: 190 bytes remaining
old guard (length + 2): 102 > 190 = false   ← missed bailout: does unnecessary JSON.stringify
new guard (byteLength + 2): 302 > 190 = true  ← correct bailout
```

**Regression — ASCII unchanged** (all 3 scenarios agree):

```
短 ASCII: old=false new=false actual=7 limit=10   agree ✅
长 ASCII: old=true  new=true  actual=502 limit=100 agree ✅
emoji:    old=true  new=true  actual=202 limit=50  agree ✅
```

**Unit tests**:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/json-utf8-bytes.test.ts \
  src/agents/session-tool-result-guard.test.ts \
  src/gateway/worker-environments/inference.test.ts \
  src/agents/harness/tool-result-middleware.test.ts
```

```
Test Files  6 passed (6)
     Tests  105 passed (105)
```

**Diff**: 2 files, +20/-1. No pnpm-lock.yaml. Branch from upstream/main (e9e62b563).

AI-assisted.
